intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and a drink at the in-water bar.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and a small waterfall. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape.

experiences.name: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe with a certified glacier guide. Trek across stunning ice formations, peer into brilliant blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This guided hike offers an unforgettable encounter with Iceland's raw natural power.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Trek
experiences.description: Hike through Iceland's surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at the base camp. The vivid landscape of red, green, yellow, and purple volcanic rock is unlike anywhere else on Earth, making this a bucket-list nature experience.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel. Rest and recover from the flight during the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in early if possible at Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10, or store luggage and take a gentle walk along the harbour front to get oriented. Siglufjörður is a charming small fishing town nestled in a dramatic fjord — explore the colourful wooden houses and the quiet harbour area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and rest after the long travel day. As darkness falls (which comes early in January), step outside or find a dark spot near the harbour to watch for the Northern Lights — January skies in northern Iceland offer excellent aurora opportunities. Dress in all your warmest layers.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,000–1,500 ISK for a pastry and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or snacks from a Reykjavik Bonus or Krónan supermarket before heading north to save money on the road.
meals.dinner: Visit Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður for a local meal — try the fish soup, a hearty and affordable Icelandic staple (around 2,500–3,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: January days in Siglufjörður are very short — expect only 4–5 hours of daylight. The road north can be icy and subject to closures; check road.is before driving. Consider renting a 4WD vehicle for safety. Budget tip: buy groceries at a Reykjavik supermarket (Bonus or Krónan) before leaving the capital as prices are significantly lower than in small towns.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður, one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums. It tells the fascinating story of the herring boom that made this remote town one of the busiest fishing ports in the North Atlantic. Entry is around 2,000 ISK — well worth it for the immersive exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or walk along the fjord shoreline toward the old fish factory ruins at the edge of town. The dramatic mountain walls rising directly from the fjord are stunning even in winter light. If conditions allow, walk the short trail up toward the lower slopes for panoramic views over the town and frozen fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunt from the hillside above town or the harbour pier. Siglufjörður's remote location means very little light pollution — one of the best spots in Iceland for aurora viewing. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app and head out when activity is rated 3 or above.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased in Reykjavik — oats, yoghurt, bread, and skyr are budget-friendly Icelandic staples.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel — sandwiches with Icelandic cheese or smoked lamb.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel kitchen if available, or visit the local Við Árbakkann café for soup and bread (around 1,800–2,500 ISK).

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — call ahead or check online. Wear microspikes or crampons for icy walking paths. The aurora forecast for northern Iceland in January is generally good; cloud cover is the main obstacle, so check the weather forecast hourly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the scenic 30-minute route through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and along the coast to Ólafsfjörður, a neighbouring fishing village. Explore the small town, its harbour, and the dramatic mountain scenery surrounding it. The drive itself through the tunnel and along the fjord is a highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving south along Route 76 to Dalvík, a larger town on Eyjafjörður. Visit the Hvoll Museum (Byggðasafnið Hvoll) which includes a quirky exhibit on the tallest man in Iceland. Walk along the Dalvík harbour and enjoy views across the wide fjord toward Akureyri.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark (around 16:00). Spend the evening watching for Northern Lights from the hotel or a dark hillside. If skies are clear, this is prime aurora territory.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — skyr with granola and coffee.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station in Dalvík or Ólafsfjörður for a budget hot dog (pylsa) — Iceland's iconic cheap eat at around 500–700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — pasta with canned fish or lamb stew made from supermarket ingredients.

day_by_day.notes: Total driving for the day is approximately 80–100 km round trip. Roads can be icy and mountain passes may close — always check road.is before departing. Dalvík is also the ferry departure point for Hrísey island and Grímsey, though these are not recommended in winter on a budget trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður to Akureyri (approximately 1 hour via the Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Route 1). Akureyri is Iceland's second-largest city and the capital of the north. Explore the charming town centre, including the famous heart-shaped traffic lights and the colourful main shopping street Hafnarstræti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — free entry and surprisingly beautiful even in winter with snow-covered sculptures and evergreen plantings. Then walk up to the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church for panoramic views over the fjord. Browse the local shops and the Bonus supermarket to restock supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a geothermally heated public pool with hot tubs and a water slide. Entry is around 1,000–1,200 ISK, making it one of Iceland's best budget experiences. Return to Siglufjörður in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Visit Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri for a traditional Icelandic lunch — fish and chips or lamb soup at around 2,000–3,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Pick up groceries at Bonus in Akureyri (significantly cheaper than Siglufjörður) and cook dinner at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 75 km from Siglufjörður. Stock up on groceries at Bonus in Akureyri — it is the cheapest supermarket chain in Iceland. The swimming pool is a beloved local institution and a great way to experience authentic Icelandic culture on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Akureyri along Route 1 to the Goðafoss waterfall (approximately 45 minutes from Akureyri, 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Goðafoss — the Waterfall of the Gods — is one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls and is free to visit. In January, the surrounding landscape is often snow-covered and the falls may be partially frozen, creating a magical scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Lake Mývatn (approximately 1 hour from Goðafoss). Explore the surreal volcanic landscape around the lake — visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations (free), the Hverfjall volcanic crater (free to walk around), and the Námaskarð geothermal area with its bubbling mud pools and steaming fumaroles (free).
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and much cheaper at around 5,500 ISK. The experience of bathing in warm mineral-rich water under a potentially aurora-lit sky is unforgettable. Return to Siglufjörður (approximately 2 hours).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at hotel before the long drive.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Goðafoss or Dimmuborgir — thermos of hot soup or sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Grab a bowl of lamb soup at the Mývatn Nature Baths café before the drive back, or cook at the hotel upon return.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — approximately 250–300 km round trip. Start early to maximise the limited daylight hours. The Mývatn Nature Baths are open until 22:00, making an evening soak very feasible. Roads in this area can be challenging in January — 4WD strongly recommended. Book Mývatn Nature Baths in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Siglufjörður. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Take a slow morning walk through the town, visiting the small local church and the old wooden buildings near the harbour. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) for a warm soak — entry around 900–1,100 ISK.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upper reaches of the Siglufjörður valley on foot or by car. The valley narrows dramatically as you head inland, with towering snow-covered peaks on either side. Look for Arctic foxes, which are sometimes spotted in the area in winter. Visit the small ski area above town if it is operating.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights vigil from the hotel or a dark spot outside town. Prepare a warm flask of hot chocolate and dress in full winter gear. If the aurora forecast is high (KP 3+), drive a few kilometres out of town to escape any residual light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — scrambled eggs, toast, and Icelandic skyr.
meals.lunch: Self-catered — hearty homemade soup using vegetables and lamb from the supermarket.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to dinner at Hannes Boy — try the catch of the day or the lamb dish (around 3,000–4,500 ISK for a main course).

day_by_day.notes: A rest day is important on a long winter trip in Iceland. The cold, short days and long drives can be exhausting. Use this day to recharge, do laundry, and plan the remaining days. Check the aurora forecast for the week ahead and plan your most active aurora-hunting nights accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west from Siglufjörður along the dramatic coastal road (Route 76) toward Hofsós. The drive hugs the coastline with stunning views of the Skagafjörður fjord. Stop at Hofsós to visit the Icelandic Emigration Centre (Vesturfarasetrið), which tells the story of Icelanders who emigrated to North America in the 19th century (entry around 1,500 ISK).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south into the Skagafjörður valley, known as Iceland's horse country. Stop to observe Icelandic horses in their natural winter environment — these sturdy, friendly horses are often seen near the road. Visit the historic Glaumbær turf farm museum (check winter hours — may be closed or have limited access in January).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the inland Route 75 through the Skagafjörður valley, then north on Route 76. The return journey offers different scenery. Watch for Northern Lights on the drive back through the dark countryside.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station in Sauðárkrókur (the main town in Skagafjörður) for a hot dog and coffee.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — fish stew or pasta.

day_by_day.notes: Total driving approximately 150–180 km. Hofsós also has a famous infinity swimming pool overlooking the fjord, but it may be closed in January — check ahead. Sauðárkrókur has a Krónan supermarket if you need to restock. The Skagafjörður area is one of Iceland's most scenic and least-visited regions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Siglufjörður toward the Tröllaskagi peninsula interior. Take Route 82 south from Ólafsfjörður toward Grenivík on the eastern shore of Eyjafjörður. The mountain road through the peninsula (if open in winter) offers spectacular views — check road.is carefully as this route can close in bad weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Grenivík and the nearby Laufás turf farm (check winter opening hours). Continue south to Akureyri for a second visit — explore the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri, entry around 1,500 ISK) and the Christmas Garden (Jólahúsið), which is open year-round and free to browse.
day_by_day.evening: Soak again at the Akureyri Swimming Pool before the drive back to Siglufjörður. The hot tubs are particularly enjoyable on cold January evenings. Return to Siglufjörður by 20:00–21:00.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Visit Strikið restaurant in Akureyri for their budget lunch special — a soup and bread combo for around 1,800–2,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel using Akureyri Bonus groceries.

day_by_day.notes: The mountain road through Tröllaskagi (Route 82 over the pass) is often closed in winter — have an alternative route via the tunnel ready. This peninsula is one of Iceland's most dramatic landscapes and worth exploring even if you must take the coastal road. Keep an eye on weather forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Full aurora-focused morning rest — sleep in after a late-night aurora watch. Spend the morning reviewing photos, journaling, and planning. Visit the Siglufjörður swimming pool for a morning soak and to chat with locals — Icelanders are very friendly and the pool is a great place to practice a few words of Icelandic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive north along the coast to the very tip of the Tröllaskagi peninsula toward Ólafsfjörður and beyond to explore the dramatic coastal scenery. Stop at viewpoints overlooking the Arctic Ocean. Look for seabirds including eider ducks and potentially white-tailed eagles along the shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Set up an aurora watch station on the hillside above Siglufjörður with a clear northern horizon. Bring a tripod if you have one for long-exposure photography. The KP index in January can produce vivid green and purple aurora displays visible to the naked eye.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered late breakfast — pancakes with Icelandic butter and jam.
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch for the coastal drive.
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty dinner — lamb chops or fish fillets from the supermarket cooked at the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: January 24 is approaching the new moon phase, which means darker skies and better aurora viewing conditions. Plan your most ambitious aurora hunt for nights around the new moon. The Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) provides the best local aurora forecasts — check it every few hours.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east from Akureyri along Route 1 toward the Fnjóskadalur valley. Turn north on Route 835 to visit Vaglaskógur, one of Iceland's largest birch forests — a surprisingly lush and peaceful spot even in winter. Walk the forest trails and enjoy the silence of the snow-covered woodland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Aldeyjarfoss waterfall in the northern highlands (accessible via Route 842 — check road conditions carefully as this F-road may be impassable in winter). If the road is closed, visit the Fosshóll area instead and walk along the Skjálfandafljót river. Return toward Akureyri and head back north to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the Akureyri Swimming Pool for a warm soak on the way back. Arrive in Siglufjörður by early evening. Aurora watch from the harbour if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel.
meals.lunch: Packed thermos lunch in the forest or by the river.
meals.dinner: Visit Við Árbakkann café in Siglufjörður for fish and chips or lamb soup.

day_by_day.notes: Aldeyjarfoss is one of Iceland's most dramatic and least-visited waterfalls, featuring basalt columns and a powerful cascade. However, Route 842 is often impassable in January — always check road.is. If closed, Vaglaskógur forest alone makes for a wonderful half-day excursion. Budget tip: pack a thermos of hot coffee and soup every day to avoid expensive café stops.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Siglufjörður in depth — visit the upper part of the town and the old ski lodge area. The Siglufjörður ski area (Skíðasvæðið) is one of Iceland's oldest and most charming, with a few lifts and runs on the mountain above town. A day ski pass is around 4,000–5,000 ISK — a fun and affordable winter activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: If not skiing, take a snowshoe walk (rent snowshoes locally if available) up the valley behind the town. The views from even a modest elevation are spectacular — the fjord below, the mountains all around, and on clear days, a view toward the open Arctic Ocean. Return to town for a warm drink.
day_by_day.evening: Final major aurora hunt of the trip. Drive 5–10 km out of Siglufjörður toward the Héðinsfjörður tunnel entrance for a completely dark sky location. Bring warm drinks, snacks, and patience. On a clear night with KP 3+, the Northern Lights here can be extraordinary — dancing green curtains reflected in the dark fjord waters.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — a big warming breakfast before outdoor activities.
meals.lunch: Hot dog and coffee at the ski lodge or a packed lunch.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a final special dinner at Hannes Boy — the fish of the day with Icelandic bread and butter (budget around 4,000–5,500 ISK for a full meal).

day_by_day.notes: Check the ski area's operating schedule in advance — it may only operate on weekends or when conditions are right. The Héðinsfjörður area outside the tunnel is one of the darkest and most remote spots accessible by car in this region — perfect for aurora photography. Dress in your absolute warmest layers for the evening vigil.

day_by_day.morning: Pack up and check out of Hotel Siglunes. Take a final walk along the Siglufjörður harbour, saying goodbye to this beautiful remote town. Drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 4.5–5 hours via Route 1 and the Ring Road). Stop at Goðafoss waterfall again if time allows — it looks different in different light conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Reykjavik in the early afternoon. Check into a budget hostel (Kex Hostel, Loft Hostel, or Bus Hostel are all well-regarded options at 4,000–7,000 ISK per night for a dorm bed). Drop bags and explore the Reykjavik city centre — walk Laugavegur shopping street, visit Hallgrímskirkja church (free exterior, tower entry around 1,000 ISK), and stroll down to the old harbour.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Sundhöll Reykjavíkur — the oldest public swimming pool in Reykjavik, recently renovated, with beautiful hot tubs. Entry around 1,100 ISK. Afterwards, explore the Reykjavik nightlife area around Austurstræti — even on a budget, a single craft beer at a local bar is a fun way to experience the city's famous nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before checkout.
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station N1 or Orkan on the Ring Road for a budget hot dog and coffee (around 600–800 ISK).
meals.dinner: Visit Hlöllabátar (Subway-style Icelandic sandwich shop) on Laugavegur for a filling and affordable meal around 1,500–2,000 ISK, or try Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the famous hot dog stand near the harbour (500 ISK per hot dog).

day_by_day.notes: Book Reykjavik accommodation in advance even in January. The drive from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik is long but straightforward on the Ring Road. If you want one more hot spring experience, the Secret Lagoon in Flúðir (about 1.5 hours from Reykjavik) is a budget-friendly alternative to the Blue Lagoon at around 3,500 ISK — consider a detour if time allows.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If your flight is in the afternoon or evening, use the morning to visit any remaining Reykjavik sights — the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands, entry around 2,000 ISK) gives excellent context for everything you have seen on the trip. Alternatively, visit the Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) on weekends for cheap Icelandic souvenirs and local food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Keflavik International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavik by Flybus, around 3,500 ISK one way). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. If you have time before the airport, the Blue Lagoon is located near Keflavik — book in advance as it sells out, but note that entry starts at around 9,000–12,000 ISK, which may stretch the budget.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with memories of the Northern Lights dancing over Siglufjörður, the steam rising from geothermal pools, the dramatic winter landscapes, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel or a bakery stop — Brauð & Co on Frakkastígur is excellent for fresh Icelandic pastries at around 500–800 ISK each.
meals.lunch: Final Icelandic hot dog at Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur near the harbour — a beloved tradition.
meals.dinner: Airport meal at Keflavik — budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK for a meal at the airport restaurants, or bring snacks from the city.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the trip: accommodation at Hotel Siglunes (11 nights) plus 1 night Reykjavik hostel; car rental (4WD essential) approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK per day; fuel approximately 3,000–5,000 ISK per day; food approximately 3,000–5,000 ISK per day if self-catering most meals; activities approximately 2,000–5,000 ISK per day. Total estimated budget: 180,000–250,000 ISK (approximately £1,000–£1,400 / $1,200–$1,700 USD) excluding flights. The Northern Lights, waterfalls, geothermal areas, and dramatic landscapes are largely free — Iceland rewards the budget traveller who is willing to explore independently.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or rent a car for the long drive north to Siglufjörður (approx. 5–6 hours). Stop in Reykjavik briefly for supplies and breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north via Route 1 and Route 76 through the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes, freshen up, and take a gentle stroll around the charming harbor town to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Settle in for a quiet first evening. Step outside or join a short local walk to scan the sky for the Northern Lights — Siglufjörður's remote location and minimal light pollution make it an excellent spot for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at a café in Reykjavik during your stopover — try Sandholt Bakery for fresh pastries and coffee (mid-range, ~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Pack a road-trip lunch from a Bonus or Krónan supermarket in Reykjavik to eat en route and save budget
meals.dinner: Dine at Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — a beloved local spot serving fresh Icelandic fish and lamb dishes (~3,500–5,500 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Keflavik to Siglufjörður is approximately 380 km and takes 5–6 hours. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. January roads in northern Iceland can be icy — a 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Arrive before dark (sunset around 16:00 in January).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður — one of Iceland's best regional museums, telling the story of the town's booming herring industry. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the beautifully restored warehouses and exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic coastal road along the Tröllaskagi peninsula toward Hofsós (approx. 45 min). Visit the Hofsós Infinity Pool — a geothermal swimming pool dramatically perched above the fjord with stunning mountain views. Soak and relax in the warm waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. After dinner, head out for Northern Lights watching from the harbor or the hillside above town. Bring warm layers and a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes or pick up fresh bread and skyr from the local Samkaup grocery store
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Herring Era Museum café or pack sandwiches for the drive to Hofsós
meals.dinner: Return to Hannes Boy or try Kaffi Rauðka, a cozy café-bar in Siglufjörður serving soups, burgers, and local beers (~2,500–4,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Hofsós Pool entry is approximately 1,000–1,200 ISK. Bring a swimsuit and towel. The Herring Era Museum costs around 2,000 ISK. Check aurora forecasts at en.vedur.is — a KP index of 3+ with clear skies gives good viewing chances.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 and Route 1 toward Akureyri (approx. 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Explore Iceland's 'Capital of the North' — visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church, stroll the pedestrian shopping street Hafnarstræti, and browse local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, peaceful even in winter. Then head to the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) for a soak in the geothermally heated outdoor pools and hot tubs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before the drive back to Siglufjörður. Alternatively, stay the night in Akureyri if road conditions are poor after dark.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before departing
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — a charming spot with soups, sandwiches, and cakes (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dine at Strikið restaurant in Akureyri for elevated Icelandic cuisine with fjord views (~4,500–7,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is approximately 90 km from Siglufjörður via Route 82. The Akureyri pool costs around 1,000 ISK. Check road conditions carefully for the return drive — Route 82 through the Vaðlaheiði tunnel (toll ~1,500 ISK) is safer than the mountain pass in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning snowshoe or winter hike in the mountains above Siglufjörður. The trails above town offer dramatic views of the fjord and surrounding peaks. Alternatively, rent cross-country skis locally if conditions allow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ólafsfjörður (approx. 20 min via the Héðinsfjörður tunnel) and explore this quiet neighboring fishing village. Walk along the harbor and enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery. Visit the local swimming pool for a warm soak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Dedicated Northern Lights watch from a dark spot outside town — try driving a few kilometers up the valley road for minimal light interference. Set an alarm for midnight if aurora activity is forecast.

meals.breakfast: Skyr, oatmeal, and coffee at Hotel Siglunes or self-catered from the grocery store
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches for the hike or drive
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal in the hotel room if facilities allow, or dine at Kaffi Rauðka for hearty comfort food (~2,500–4,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: January hiking in Iceland requires proper winter gear — crampons, waterproof layers, and a headlamp are essential. Ólafsfjörður tunnel toll is approximately 1,000 ISK. The Ólafsfjörður pool costs around 900–1,100 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along Route 1 toward Lake Mývatn (approx. 2.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Stop at Goðafoss waterfall en route — one of Iceland's most beautiful waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Mývatn. Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but less crowded and more affordable. Soak in the mineral-rich blue-green waters surrounded by volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the eerie Dimmuborgir lava formations and Hverfjall volcanic crater rim (if safe and accessible). Return to Siglufjörður or consider staying overnight near Mývatn to maximize time in the area.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before the drive
meals.lunch: Café at Mývatn Nature Baths or bring packed lunch to eat at Goðafoss
meals.dinner: Dine at Vogafjós Farm Restaurant near Mývatn — famous for fresh geothermal bread, smoked trout, and farm-to-table Icelandic dishes (~4,000–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths entry is approximately 5,500–6,500 ISK. Book in advance online. Goðafoss is accessible year-round but paths can be icy — wear crampons. The round trip from Siglufjörður to Mývatn is about 5 hours of driving total, so an early start is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Siglufjörður. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and explore the town's small art galleries and the Segull 67 craft brewery for a morning tour and tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sauðárkrókur (approx. 1 hour south via Route 75) — the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum and explore the town. Stop at a local swimming pool for a warm soak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Northern Lights watch from the harbor — the fjord's reflective water can create stunning mirror-image aurora displays on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café in Sauðárkrókur — try Kaffi Krókur for homemade soups and sandwiches (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hannes Boy in Siglufjörður — try the pan-fried Arctic char or lamb soup (~3,500–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Segull 67 brewery tours should be booked in advance. The Skagafjörður Heritage Museum costs approximately 1,500–2,000 ISK. January days are very short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~16:00) so plan driving during daylight hours.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing from the Siglufjörður/Akureyri area. Professional guides use real-time aurora forecasts and cloud cover maps to find the best viewing locations. Tours typically depart in the late afternoon but some operators offer full-evening experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Before the evening tour, spend the afternoon visiting the Tröllaskagi peninsula's scenic viewpoints. Drive the coastal road toward Dalvík (approx. 30 min from Akureyri) for panoramic fjord and mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — experience the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky in vivid greens and purples, guided by an expert who explains the science and mythology behind the phenomenon. Tours typically run 3–4 hours.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Siglunes
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Dalvík or packed meal from the grocery store
meals.dinner: Pre-tour dinner at a restaurant in Akureyri or Siglufjörður — fuel up with a hearty lamb stew or fish dish (~3,500–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights tours cost approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK per person. Book in advance through operators like Arctic Adventures or local Akureyri-based companies. Tours are weather-dependent and reputable operators offer free rebooking if conditions are poor. Dress in your warmest layers.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the long drive south toward the Golden Circle and South Iceland (approx. 5–6 hours from Siglufjörður to Reykjavik area). Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls in West Iceland if routing via Route 1 and Route 50.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament, the Alþingi.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a guesthouse or hotel near Selfoss or Reykjavik for the next few nights. Explore the area and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Siglunes before the long drive
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside café or petrol station restaurant en route — Kaffi Kjöt in Borgarnes is a good mid-route option (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in Selfoss — try Tryggvaskáli for Icelandic classics in a historic setting (~4,000–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day with significant driving. Check road.is for conditions on all routes. Þingvellir National Park entry is free; parking costs approximately 750 ISK. Consider booking accommodation near the Golden Circle in advance for the next 2–3 nights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approx. 1 hour from Selfoss). Soak in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, dating to 1891, surrounded by geothermal geysers and steaming vents. A more intimate and authentic experience than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle route: visit Geysir geothermal area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes, then drive to the magnificent Gullfoss waterfall — Iceland's most iconic cascade, partially frozen in January.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your South Iceland base. If aurora forecast is favorable, drive to a dark area near Þingvellir or the countryside for Northern Lights viewing.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a local bakery
meals.lunch: Café at Geysir Center — Geysir Bistro offers soups and sandwiches with views of the geothermal field (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friðheimar greenhouse restaurant near Reykholt — famous for tomato-based dishes grown in geothermal greenhouses (~4,500–7,000 ISK, book ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approximately 3,500–4,500 ISK. Book online in advance. Gullfoss and Geysir are free to visit. Paths at Gullfoss can be extremely icy in January — crampons are essential. Friðheimar requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the South Coast. Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall (you can walk behind it in summer, but in January enjoy the dramatic ice formations from the front) and Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches with towering basalt columns, sea stacks, and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village of Vík. If skies are clear, the black sand beach area offers excellent Northern Lights viewing with the sea stacks as a dramatic foreground. Return to your South Iceland accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat at Skógafoss or grab food at the Skógar Museum café (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Suður-Vík restaurant in Vík — cozy spot serving fish and chips, lamb, and Icelandic comfort food (~3,500–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara — sneaker waves are deadly and claim lives every year. Stay well back from the waterline. Seljalandsfoss path may be closed due to ice in January. All waterfalls are free to visit; parking fees apply (~750 ISK).

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Skaftafell in Vatnajökull National Park (approx. 2 hours east of Vík). Join a Vatnajökull Glacier Hike with a certified glacier guide — strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe, walking across blue ice and past crevasses and ice caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike, visit the nearby Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — a breathtaking lake filled with floating icebergs calved from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier. Walk to Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash up on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back west toward Reykjavik (approx. 3.5–4 hours). Stop for dinner en route or in Reykjavik. Check in to Reykjavik accommodation for the final nights.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the drive — pack snacks for the glacier hike
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch for the glacier hike (guides recommend this) or eat at the Skaftafell visitor center café
meals.dinner: Dinner in Reykjavik upon arrival — try Messinn for excellent pan-fried fish in a casual, mid-range setting (~4,000–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hike tours cost approximately 8,000–12,000 ISK per person. Book well in advance through Icelandic Mountain Guides or Arctic Adventures. Tours last 3–4 hours and require moderate fitness. All equipment is provided. Jökulsárlón is free to visit. This is a long day — start early.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa near Keflavik (book the Premium or Comfort package for in-water massages and silica mud masks). Soak in the iconic milky-blue 38–40°C waters surrounded by volcanic lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik. Explore the city: visit Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the top for panoramic views), the Harpa Concert Hall, and the colorful old harbor district. Browse the shops on Laugavegur street.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — join an evening Northern Lights boat tour from Reykjavik harbor or drive to the Grótta lighthouse peninsula for aurora viewing with the city skyline as a backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Reykjavik hotel or guesthouse
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon's in-water bar (included in some packages) or at a café in Reykjavik upon return (~2,500–4,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) in Reykjavik — celebrating Icelandic ingredients with a modern twist (~6,000–9,000 ISK per person for a special occasion)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be booked weeks in advance — it sells out quickly. Comfort package costs approximately 14,000–18,000 ISK. Arrive at your booked time slot. The Grótta lighthouse is a 20-minute walk from central Reykjavik and is one of the best free aurora spots in the city.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavik. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history and culture. Browse the gift shop for quality souvenirs — Icelandic wool products, lava salt, and local spirits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute shopping on Laugavegur. Visit the Reykjavik Flea Market (Kolaportið) if open — a great place for affordable Icelandic goods and local snacks. Head to Keflavik Airport (45 min from Reykjavik) with plenty of time before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with memories of aurora-lit skies, steaming hot springs, and dramatic volcanic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast at your hotel — enjoy skyr with berries, smoked salmon, and rye bread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic food including hákarl (fermented shark), rye bread ice cream, and lamb soup (~2,500–4,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Keflavik International Airport or grab snacks for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the drive to Keflavik and airport security. Return your rental car with a full tank — petrol stations near the airport include N1 and Orkan. The National Museum costs approximately 2,500 ISK. Kolaportið flea market is open weekends only.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the Aurora Borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and steam caves while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the lagoon, a silica mud mask, and a drink at the in-water bar.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and a small waterfall. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a more intimate connection with Iceland's geothermal landscape.

experiences.name: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the largest glacier in Europe with a certified glacier guide. Trek across stunning ice formations, peer into brilliant blue crevasses, and learn about Iceland's rapidly changing glacial landscape. This guided hike offers an unforgettable encounter with Iceland's raw natural power.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Trek
experiences.description: Hike through Iceland's surreal rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at the base camp. The vivid landscape of red, green, yellow, and purple volcanic rock is unlike anywhere else on Earth, making this a bucket-list nature experience.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Transfer via private luxury vehicle to Reykjavík for a brief orientation stop before beginning the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður. The drive (approx. 5–6 hours) winds through dramatic lava fields and snow-dusted mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north along Route 1 and then Route 76 through the Tröllaskagi Peninsula. Stop at Hofsós Infinity Pool — a geothermal pool perched dramatically above Skagafjörður fjord — for a warm, restorative soak after the long journey. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Check in and settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Hotel Siglunes' own restaurant, renowned for locally sourced Arctic char and lamb. After dinner, step outside or join a short guided walk along the harbor to scan the skies for the Northern Lights — Siglufjörður's minimal light pollution makes it an exceptional aurora-viewing location.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Keflavík Airport lounge (Icelandair Saga Lounge) before departure or en route snacks in the private transfer vehicle
meals.lunch: Stop at Gauksmýri Lodge Restaurant near Hvammstangi — a charming farm-to-table spot serving hearty Icelandic lamb soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes Restaurant — Arctic char with dill butter, slow-roasted Icelandic lamb, and skyr panna cotta for dessert; pair with Icelandic craft beer or a curated wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. The drive to Siglufjörður can be affected by winter road conditions — check road.is before departing. Pack warm layers accessible in carry-on for the outdoor aurora viewing. Request a fjord-view room at Hotel Siglunes for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely gourmet breakfast at Hotel Siglunes. After breakfast, take a self-guided walk through Siglufjörður's charming harbor town — explore the colorful wooden houses, the old herring factory district, and the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið), one of Iceland's finest regional museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Herring Era Museum in depth — a fascinating multi-building complex that recreates the boom years of the 20th-century herring industry. Afterward, take a scenic drive along the fjord to the nearby village of Ólafsfjörður through the twin tunnels, stopping at viewpoints to photograph the dramatic winter fjord landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður for a Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a local expert guide who monitors aurora forecasts and drives to optimal dark-sky locations around the fjord and surrounding mountains. Wrap up with hot cocoa and Icelandic spirits back at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic breakfast at Hotel Siglunes — skyr with berries, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cozy café serving homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and freshly baked pastries
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes Restaurant — pan-seared cod with langoustine bisque, followed by Icelandic cheese board and cloudberry jam

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have limited winter hours — confirm opening times in advance. Aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions and cloud cover; the guide will monitor forecasts throughout the day. Dress in full thermal layers for the evening tour.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snowshoe or winter hiking excursion on the slopes above Siglufjörður with a local mountain guide. The trails offer breathtaking panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding peaks. In winter, the area is blanketed in snow, creating a pristine Arctic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south along the Tröllaskagi Peninsula to the Hofsós Infinity Pool for a second, more leisurely geothermal soak. The pool's heated waters (38–40°C) contrast beautifully with the cold winter air and fjord views. Spend 1–2 hours relaxing before returning to Siglufjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-hotel aurora alert service — the hotel staff monitors aurora forecasts and wakes guests when activity is high. Enjoy a premium dinner at the hotel, then retire to your room or step onto the terrace for aurora viewing with a glass of Icelandic schnapps.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — warm oatmeal porridge with Icelandic honey, smoked lamb, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic prepared by Hotel Siglunes — thermos of lamb soup, artisan sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes Restaurant — reindeer tenderloin with root vegetable purée and juniper berry sauce, paired with a premium Burgundy red

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe rental and guide can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Hofsós Pool is approximately 45 minutes south of Siglufjörður — confirm winter opening hours. January days are very short (sunrise ~11:00, sunset ~15:30), so plan outdoor activities around the limited daylight window.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east along the scenic Eyjafjörður fjord toward Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North' (approx. 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Explore Akureyri's charming town center: visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, browse the botanical garden (Lystigarðurinn), and stroll the pedestrian shopping street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for a curated look at Icelandic contemporary art. Afterward, take a short drive to Kjarnaskógur forest — Iceland's largest urban forest — for a peaceful winter walk among snow-covered birch trees.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Rub23 in Akureyri — one of Iceland's finest restaurants, celebrated for its innovative sushi and premium Icelandic seafood. Return to Siglufjörður after dinner, keeping an eye on the skies for aurora activity on the drive back through the dark fjord roads.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, Icelandic yogurt parfait, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Bautinn Restaurant in Akureyri — a beloved local institution serving traditional Icelandic lamb and fish dishes in a warm, rustic setting
meals.dinner: Rub23, Akureyri — Arctic char sashimi, langoustine tempura, and wagyu beef with truffle; premium sake or Icelandic craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions on Route 82 and Route 1 before driving. Akureyri is a worthwhile full-day excursion from Siglufjörður. The return drive at night offers excellent aurora-viewing opportunities — pull over safely at designated viewpoints if the lights appear.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated aurora photography morning — if the previous nights yielded strong displays, use this morning to review and edit images. Otherwise, take a guided ice fishing experience on a frozen lake near Siglufjörður, arranged through the hotel. A local guide provides all equipment and teaches traditional Icelandic ice fishing techniques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Centre (Þjóðlagasetur) to learn about Iceland's rich musical heritage. Afterward, enjoy a private guided tour of the town's historic wooden architecture with a local historian, learning about the herring boom era that shaped the town.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — second dedicated aurora tour with a professional guide, venturing further into the mountains above the fjord for optimal dark-sky conditions. The guide uses real-time aurora forecast apps and has intimate knowledge of the best local vantage points.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full Icelandic spread with hákarl (fermented shark) tasting for the adventurous, alongside more familiar options
meals.lunch: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) pop-up style lunch at the hotel — langoustine soup and fresh fish skewers
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — five-course tasting menu featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients: langoustine, Arctic char, lamb, skyr mousse, and Icelandic cheese

day_by_day.notes: Ice fishing requires advance booking through the hotel concierge. The five-course tasting menu at Hotel Siglunes should be reserved at least 24 hours in advance. January is statistically one of the best months for aurora activity in northern Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður early for a full-day excursion to the Mývatn region (approx. 2.5 hours east). Begin at the Mývatn Nature Baths — a premium geothermal lagoon experience in a stunning volcanic landscape. Soak in the mineral-rich blue waters with far fewer crowds than the Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the extraordinary volcanic landscape around Lake Mývatn: visit the Dimmuborgir lava formations (dramatic black lava pillars and arches), the Hverfjall tephra crater, and the Námaskarð geothermal area with its bubbling mud pools and steaming fumaroles.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Vogafjós Farm Restaurant near Mývatn — a unique farm-to-table experience where you can watch cows being milked through a glass window while dining on fresh dairy products, smoked trout, and Icelandic lamb. Return to Siglufjörður overnight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — quick but hearty breakfast before early departure: skyr, rye bread with smoked salmon, and coffee to go
meals.lunch: Gamli Bærinn at Mývatn — a cozy local restaurant serving lamb soup, fish stew, and homemade bread
meals.dinner: Vogafjós Farm Restaurant — fresh mozzarella made on-site, smoked trout, slow-cooked lamb, and geysir bread (rye bread baked underground using geothermal heat)

day_by_day.notes: The Mývatn Nature Baths are less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and offer a more authentic experience — book tickets in advance. The drive back to Siglufjörður after dinner will be in complete darkness; drive carefully on Route 1 and check road conditions. This is a long day — consider an early start.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Take a gentle walk along the Siglufjörður harbor waterfront, watching local fishing boats and enjoying the dramatic fjord scenery. Visit the town's small but charming local shops for Icelandic wool products (lopapeysa sweaters) and artisan crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury spa afternoon at Hotel Siglunes — arrange an in-room massage or spa treatment through the hotel. Alternatively, visit the local Siglufjörður swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a geothermally heated community pool with hot tubs, beloved by locals.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 15:30) photography session from the harbor or hillside above town. As darkness falls, enjoy a premium cocktail hour at the hotel bar before a special dinner. Keep aurora alerts active for a potential late-night viewing session.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — extended leisurely breakfast with all Icelandic specialties, fresh pastries, and unlimited coffee
meals.lunch: Húsið Restaurant in Siglufjörður — a local favorite serving fresh fish of the day, lamb burgers, and homemade cakes
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — premium seafood platter featuring langoustine, scallops, and Arctic char, with a bottle of premier cru Chablis

day_by_day.notes: The local swimming pool is an authentic Icelandic experience and costs very little — a wonderful contrast to the luxury hotel. Arrange spa treatments at least one day in advance. This rest day is important given the active schedule of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the Golden Circle region (approx. 5–6 hours from Siglufjörður, with an overnight stay planned in the south). Depart early and stop at Goðafoss Waterfall — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations along its edges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south to Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk through the dramatic Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi) established here in 930 AD. Check into a luxury accommodation in the Golden Circle area for the night.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ion Adventure Hotel's Lava Restaurant — one of Iceland's most architecturally stunning dining venues, built into a lava field with panoramic views. After dinner, join a Northern Lights tour from the hotel's prime dark-sky location.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — final breakfast before checkout; packed lunch prepared by the hotel for the road
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch from Hotel Siglunes enjoyed at Goðafoss Waterfall viewpoint — thermos of soup, artisan sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Lava Restaurant at Ion Adventure Hotel — locally sourced tasting menu featuring Icelandic lamb, Arctic char, and foraged ingredients; exceptional wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day moving from north to south Iceland. Check out of Hotel Siglunes and arrange luggage transfer. Book Ion Adventure Hotel or similar luxury property (e.g., Deplar Farm, Retreat at Blue Lagoon) well in advance. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can be challenging — allow extra travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Full Golden Circle day. Begin at Geysir Geothermal Area — witness the mighty Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Explore the surrounding hot spring field with its colorful mineral pools and steaming vents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Gullfoss Waterfall — the 'Golden Falls' — one of Iceland's most iconic waterfalls, where the Hvítá river plunges into a dramatic canyon. In winter, the falls are often partially frozen, creating a spectacular ice-and-water display. Afterward, visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool (1891), a natural hot spring surrounded by geysers and hot springs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Golden Circle area accommodation. Enjoy a premium dinner and aurora monitoring. The flat, open landscape of the south provides excellent aurora viewing conditions on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Ion Adventure Hotel — full breakfast with panoramic lava field views; fresh Icelandic dairy, eggs, and smoked meats
meals.lunch: Geysir Center Restaurant — upgraded option with fresh fish soup, lamb stew, and Icelandic flatbread
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant (reservation required) — unique dining inside a geothermal tomato greenhouse; tomato soup, tomato-based dishes, and house-made tomato beer or schnapps

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is a more intimate and authentic alternative to the Blue Lagoon — book tickets in advance. Friðheimar is extremely popular and requires advance reservations. Dress in waterproof layers for Gullfoss as spray from the falls can be significant even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the South Coast. Stop at Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — walk behind the curtain of water (conditions permitting in winter) for a unique perspective. Continue to Skógafoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most photogenic falls, often with ice formations and frost crystals in January.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, with towering basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves. Afterward, explore the nearby village of Vík and its iconic clifftop church.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury hotel in the Vík or Mýrdalur area (e.g., Hotel Katla by Keahotels or a premium guesthouse). Dinner at the hotel restaurant featuring South Coast specialties. Aurora viewing from the beach or hotel grounds.

meals.breakfast: Ion Adventure Hotel — packed breakfast to go for an early start
meals.lunch: Skál! at Skógar — a farm-to-table restaurant near Skógafoss serving Icelandic lamb, fresh fish, and homemade bread
meals.dinner: Hotel Katla Restaurant — South Coast lamb with root vegetables, pan-seared Arctic char, and skyr cheesecake; local craft beer pairing

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach is genuinely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean and stay well back from the water's edge. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the falls may be closed in winter due to ice — check locally. The South Coast is one of Iceland's most scenic drives.

day_by_day.morning: Vatnajökull Glacier Hike — depart early for a guided glacier hiking experience on Europe's largest glacier. Strap on crampons and harnesses with a certified glacier guide and trek across the ancient blue ice, exploring ice caves, crevasses, and glacial formations. This is a world-class adventure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most breathtaking natural wonders, where enormous icebergs calve from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and float serenely in the lagoon. In winter, the lagoon is often partially frozen, creating a surreal icy landscape. Walk to Diamond Beach where ice chunks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Vík/South Coast area or continue toward Reykjavík. Celebratory premium dinner at a top restaurant. Aurora viewing en route if conditions permit.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Katla — hearty breakfast before the glacier hike: eggs, oatmeal, smoked salmon, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch provided by the glacier tour operator or hotel — energy bars, thermos of soup, and sandwiches consumed near the glacier
meals.dinner: Hótel Rangá Restaurant (near Hella) — one of Iceland's finest dining experiences; wild game, Icelandic lamb, and fresh fish with an exceptional wine cellar; the hotel also has a dedicated aurora alert service

day_by_day.notes: The Vatnajökull Glacier Hike requires advance booking with a certified guide company (e.g., Local Guide, Icelandic Mountain Guides). Wear warm, waterproof layers and sturdy boots — the guide provides crampons and harnesses. Jökulsárlón is approximately 370 km from Reykjavík — this is a long day. Consider staying at Hótel Rangá for the night.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula for the crown jewel of Icelandic geothermal experiences — the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa. Arrive for a premium 'Retreat Spa' package: enjoy the iconic milky-blue silica-rich waters, in-water massages, silica mud masks, algae masks, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon (the private inner lagoon). Spend 3–4 hours in total relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into The Retreat at Blue Lagoon — Iceland's most exclusive hotel, built into the lava field surrounding the lagoon with private lagoon access. Explore the hotel's stunning architecture, private spa facilities, and lava cave bar. Alternatively, drive to Reykjavík and check into a luxury city hotel (e.g., The Reykjavík EDITION or Hotel Borg).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's vibrant culinary scene. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (illuminated at night) and the Harpa Concert Hall. Enjoy a world-class dinner at one of Reykjavík's top restaurants. Final dedicated Northern Lights tour from Reykjavík's outskirts.

meals.breakfast: Hótel Rangá — full breakfast before checkout and drive to Blue Lagoon
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — dine in your bathrobe with views over the lagoon; fresh seafood, Icelandic lamb, and premium cocktails
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavík — Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant; Nordic tasting menu with wine pairing, showcasing the finest Icelandic ingredients in innovative preparations

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Retreat packages must be booked well in advance — they sell out months ahead. The Retreat at Blue Lagoon is Iceland's most exclusive accommodation and requires very early booking. Dill Restaurant also requires advance reservations. This is the penultimate day — a perfect blend of luxury relaxation and fine dining.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavík. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last walk along the Reykjavík waterfront (Ægisgarður) and visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) — a stunning stainless steel Viking ship sculpture with views across the bay to Mount Esja. Browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) or the Laugavegur shopping street for last-minute Icelandic souvenirs: lopapeysa wool sweaters, Icelandic sea salt, skyr, and local design items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) for a final immersion in Icelandic history and culture, or the Reykjavík Art Museum for contemporary Icelandic art. Enjoy a farewell lunch at one of Reykjavík's top restaurants. Transfer to Keflavík International Airport (45 minutes from Reykjavík) for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Relax in the Icelandair Saga Lounge before your flight, reflecting on 13 extraordinary days of Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, glaciers, and Arctic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel in Reykjavík — full luxury breakfast; savor the last Icelandic skyr, smoked salmon, and freshly baked rye bread
meals.lunch: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market), Reykjavík — premium Icelandic steakhouse and seafood restaurant; dry-aged Icelandic beef, langoustine, and Arctic char; a perfect farewell meal
meals.dinner: Icelandair Saga Lounge at Keflavík Airport — light refreshments and drinks before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in. Duty-free shopping at Keflavík Airport is excellent — stock up on Icelandic spirits (Brennivín), Icelandic chocolate, and beauty products from the Blue Lagoon skincare line. Confirm all bookings and transfers the evening before. This concludes a truly premium 13-day Icelandic adventure.
